name: Fijian
variant: Standard (Bauan) Fijian, the standard of books, newspapers and town speech
script: Latin (no extra letters), but with its own letter values: b = mb, d = nd, q = ngg, g = ng, c = th, dr = ndr; left to right
basis: Paul Geraghty's 'Introduction to Fijian' course syllabus (textbook Say Bula!): sounds and spelling; greetings and questions; independent and subject pronouns; suffixed, non-suffixed and nominal possession; noun phrase, 'to be' and 'to have', verb phrase
src: Paul Geraghty, Introduction to Fijian: four-week course syllabus with weekly grammar topics, textbook Say Bula! by Paul Geraghty (PDF hosted by Beijing Foreign Studies University, iss.bfsu.edu.cn; no institution, year or licence named)
Pasifika TKI (NZ Ministry of Education site), PDF file named Vosa Vakaviti Fijian Language Cards: greetings, courtesy, introductions, How are you?, family words (used to check spellings)
Albert J. Schütz, 'Fijian language' article on Fiji Guide (© 2022): Bauan as the written and town standard, Cargill's alphabet
Brigham Young University catalogue entry for FIJI 100 Language Study: Fijian (survival-level outcomes only)
Not opened: the Peace Corps Lessons in Fijian (ERIC ED131693; download refused), Schütz's Spoken Fijian and The Fijian Language on ScholarSpace (blocked by a browser check), and Say Bula! itself
note: Only the first four weeks are from a syllabus: Geraghty's order gives stage 1, the pronoun and possession lessons and the start of stage 3 ('to be' and 'to have', questions, the verb phrase). Everything after that (tense and aspect markers, negation with sega ni, transitive endings, numbers, prices, food, time, days, directions, family, commands and the village-visit lesson) is common course practice and my own judgment from general knowledge of Fijian, not from an opened source. Spellings of the greetings, courtesy, introduction and How are you? phrases and the family words follow the NZ language cards (which write Ko cei na yacamu? and Yalovinaka); Io and Sega and all other Fijian words in the titles were spelled by me and should be checked by a speaker. Nothing was opened on village protocol (sevusevu, yaqona); that lesson is from general knowledge. Device voices for fj are not checked.
hardest: Letters with unexpected sounds: b, d, q, g, c and dr (Nadi is said Nandi)
Pronouns that count: one, two, a few or many, and 'we' with or without the listener (keirau, kedaru, keitou, keda)
Several kinds of 'my': tamaqu (family, body), noqu (things), kequ (food), mequ (drink)
Verb first and subject last: E lako o Jone, with the subject pronoun before the verb as well

items: fj-sounds
Sounds and spelling: b = mb, d = nd, q = ngg, g = ng, c = th, dr
fj-vowels
Vowels and stress: five vowels, long vowels, stress near the end of the word
fj-greetings
Greetings and courtesy: Ni sa bula, Vinaka, Yalovinaka, Ni sa moce
fj-phrases
Short words and phrases: Io, Sega, Vosota, Vosoti au
fj-intro
Introducing yourself: Ko cei na yacamu? Na yacaqu ko…, Ko iko mai vei?
fj-how-are-you
How are you?: Ko vakacava tiko? Au vinaka tiko, vinaka
fj-pronouns
Independent pronouns: au, iko, koya; for two, a few and many; with or without the listener
fj-subject
Subject pronouns before the verb: au, o, e (Au lako, E lako)
fj-articles
Articles: na for things, o / ko before names (na vale, ko Jone)
fj-suffixed
Suffixed possession for family and body: tamaqu, yacamu, ligana
fj-noqu
General possession: noqu, nomu, nona (noqu vale)
fj-kequ
Possession of food and drink: kequ, kemu; mequ, memu
fj-nominal
Possession with a noun owner: na yaca ni koro
fj-numbers
Numbers and prices: dua, rua, tolu … tini; E vica?
fj-to-be
'To be' and 'to have': sentences with no verb, and e tiko (there is)
fj-questions
Question words: cava, cei, vei, vica
fj-verb-phrase
The verb phrase: verb first, subject last (E lako o Jone)
fj-tense
Tense and aspect: sa, a (past), na (future), tiko (ongoing)
fj-negation
Negation: sega ni (Au sega ni kila)
fj-transitive
Verbs with an object: -ca and -taka (raica, vakarautaka)
fj-food
Eating and asking: Au via kana, Au via gunu ti, Kerekere…
fj-time
Time and days: Sa vica na kaloko? Moniti, Tusiti … Sigatabu
fj-family
Family: tamaqu, tinaqu, tuakaqu, taciqu, ganequ
fj-directions
Directions and places: ki (to), mai (from), e (at); i matau, i mawi
fj-lets
'Let's' and commands: Daru lako, Lako mai
fj-village
Visiting a village: sevusevu and yaqona
